title: Suggestions and open questions for the owner to choose between, with the evidence that produced each
rule: nothing on this page is implemented by the tool that writes it; decision_status is set only by a human commit, so a suggestion cannot approve itself
impact_effort_note: impact, effort and risk are this session's estimates, not measurements.

suggestions.title: Publish the collector's push state, not just its run state
suggestions.why: Six consecutive scheduled runs reported `success` while the repository's own `_ci/commit.log` printed `MARKER: PUSH FAILED after 5 attempts` on every one of them. A green checkmark next to a job that landed nothing is worse than a red one, because it ends the enquiry. The site should print, per dataset, the last run whose output is actually in `git`, so 'the collector ran' and 'the data is here' are separate claims.
suggestions.path_a: A: the refresh job writes `data/pipeline/_last_push.json` (commit sha, row counts, timestamp) in the same commit as the data, and the capture page renders that file.
suggestions.path_b: B: the page derives it live from `git log --grep 'data: refresh'` at build time.
suggestions.path_c: C: leave it to the workflow annotations only.
suggestions.recommended_because: a committed file is checkable by the same verifier that checks everything else; (B) is right until a session force-pushes, and (C) is exactly the log nobody opened this time.

suggestions.title: Move the results feed's four coupled baselines in one commit, or leave the feed alone
suggestions.why: The feed says 1 of 14 Week 10 games is officially verified; the official page now prints 13 finals, and this session transcribed them (with the standings cross-checked three ways). The feed cannot simply absorb them: appending those 13 rows to the published feed makes 23 of 32 clubs disagree with the standings baseline the feed is *validated against*, and the row-count pin and the pinned mirror have scores for only 1 of the 13. Four artefacts — the transcription, the count pin, the standings baseline, the mirror re-pin — are one change or none. Today it is none, deliberately, and the discrepancy is published instead of hidden.
suggestions.path_a: A: one PR that moves all four together and re-runs every results gate, reviewed as a single diff.
suggestions.path_b: B: keep the 2026-11-14 feed frozen as a dated artefact and publish the newer read only on the capture page (this round's choice).
suggestions.path_c: C: append the finals without re-baselining (rejected: it breaks the arithmetic gate that exists to catch exactly this).
suggestions.recommended_because: (B) is safe but understates verified coverage on a page owners read as 'the feed'; (A) is a contained change if it is one commit with the gates in the same diff.

suggestions.title: Have the collector store the raw response bytes beside each capture
suggestions.why: Retention now stores a hashed transcription plus a diff, which is enough to prove the shape and to diff days. It is not enough to re-derive a field the extractor did not notice — which is the failure mode that hid the two undocumented record triples on the standings page. The fix is one line where the fetch happens, and that file is owned by open PR #61, so this session recorded the request rather than editing it.
suggestions.path_a: A: gzip each response into `data/captures/raw/<dataset>/<sha>.html.gz` and add its hash to the index line.
suggestions.path_b: B: keep text only, and accept that a new field needs a fresh read (a day's delay).
suggestions.path_c: C: store only the HTML fragment the parser consumed.
suggestions.recommended_because: the retention cost is a few hundred KB per day per dataset, and it is the only artefact that lets a future session re-parse without trusting this one's parser.

suggestions.title: Stop trusting a day-over-day injury delta until two machine reads of the same URL exist
suggestions.why: The first delta measured (2026-11-14 → 2026-11-15) produced 34 changed cells, but the two sides came from different extraction paths: the collector's parser versus a hand transcription. Two of the 34 are 'appeared' rows that only exist because one source labels the Rams `LAR` and the other `LA`. A join alias now hides that, which is the right interim answer, but a delta built across two parsers cannot distinguish a club moving a player from a page reflowing.
suggestions.path_a: A: publish day-over-day deltas only between two captures whose `pipeline_source` and schema hash match; show cross-path comparisons labelled as such.
suggestions.path_b: B: publish all deltas with the caveat sentence.
suggestions.path_c: C: wait until the collector has two consecutive green days.
suggestions.recommended_because: the surprise-not-level rule is only worth anything if the surprise is not an artefact of the reader.

suggestions.title: Register the injury-surprise model as PR-04 before scoring it
suggestions.why: The mechanism that makes PR-01 honest costs nothing to reuse: a rule file, its window and its gates committed before any evaluation. There are now exactly two dated injury captures, which is enough to write the rule and not nearly enough to fit anything to it. Registering now, with the first evaluation window opening at week 12, is what keeps the result interpretable; fitting it to these two days would produce a number that means nothing.
suggestions.path_a: A: write PR-04 (designation-change → market-adjusted margin surprise) this round, evaluate from week 12.
suggestions.path_b: B: accumulate 4 weeks of captures first, then register.
suggestions.path_c: C: skip it until the price question is answered.
suggestions.recommended_because: the window is defined by game weeks, not by how many captures happen to exist, and (B) invites the temptation to tune on the accumulated days.

suggestions.title: Print `n` and the window next to every number the site states
suggestions.why: The shadow-baseline page does this (Brier 0.224, n=117, weeks 3-10, one season) and the landing page's headline stats mostly do, but several older panels still show a percentage with no count beside it. A rate without a denominator is the single most common way this repository could mislead a reader while every input being true.
suggestions.path_a: A: extend the site checker to require an `n=` or a row count within the same element as any printed percentage.
suggestions.path_b: B: fix the known panels by hand.
suggestions.recommended_because: a gate that fires on the next page somebody writes is cheaper than an audit of the twenty already written.

suggestions.title: Pick one decision surface and archive the rest
suggestions.why: The same readiness question is currently answered on 21 pages under `pages/`, plus four parallel site trees (`app/`, `console/`, `hub/`, `site/`) and 30+ more under `live/`, `lab/`, `audit/`, `analysis/`. Every one of them is individually verified and source-linked, and a reader cannot hold twenty copies of a claim in their head, so the verification work does not convert into decisions. Divergence is already visible: `docs/analysis/` records nine open questions while `data/audit/decision_questions.json` carries four.
suggestions.path_a: A: one canonical decision page (this register + readiness), every other tree marked `archived` with a banner and a link, nothing deleted.
suggestions.path_b: B: keep all trees, add a per-page 'supersedes / superseded by' line.
suggestions.path_c: C: do nothing; the site is a record of work, not a tool.
suggestions.recommended_because: archiving keeps the audit trail (the brief values that) while telling the reader where to look, which is the part that is missing now.

suggestions.title: Make the alarm list something a reader can clear, not only read
suggestions.why: Two alarms are live (a column-count mismatch in the deficiency register, a club code outside the standings register). They are published, which is right, but nothing records that somebody looked at one, agreed it was harmless, and chose to keep it. An alarm with no disposition becomes background noise within a fortnight — which is precisely how the `_ci` comment that said 'untracked' survived next to tracked files for weeks.
suggestions.path_a: A: a `data/captures/dispositions.json` keyed by capture + violation kind, with a one-line human reason; the page shows 'acknowledged by <commit> on <date>'.
suggestions.path_b: B: issues in the tracker instead.
suggestions.recommended_because: the reason has to live next to the data it excuses, and be diffable; the store already carries `alarm_only` versus `fail_the_build`, so this is the same shape with a human answer in it.

suggestions.title: Capture inactives and snap counts as a first-class dataset with its own pins
suggestions.why: The brief asks for official inactive lists and snap counts; the retained set contains no snap share at all, so 'a backup replaced the starter' is still only confirmed where the league prints a designation, and the backup-deficiency matrix rests on depth charts instead. The pins framework is already there — the dataset simply does not exist yet.
suggestions.path_a: A: add `game_report_inactives` and `snap_counts` to the config with row-count and closure pins (32 clubs exactly once per game; Σsnap shares within tolerance), ingest retroactively for weeks 9-11.
suggestions.path_b: B: keep treating them out of scope until the collector lands green twice.
suggestions.path_c: C: derive nothing and rely on designations.
suggestions.recommended_because: the retroactive ingest is possible now and gets harder every week, and a pin written before the data arrives is the cheap version of the honesty the rest of this repo is built on.

suggestions.title: Decide, in one line, whether Game Book PDFs are in the ingestion set
suggestions.why: A real 'Download Game Book (PDF)' link exists on the official game pages — reachable from the Week 10 Chiefs-at-Falcons page — so the play-level record the brief wants as the source of actual starters is obtainable. It is also ~14 PDFs a week of parsing that no other artefact in this repository currently consumes, which makes it a scope decision rather than an engineering one.
suggestions.path_a: A: ingest play-by-play only (structured, one source), leave Game Books as the manual check for contested rows.
suggestions.path_b: B: ingest Game Books for the starter/offence columns and cross-check them against the depth charts.
suggestions.path_c: C: neither, until the availability page proves it needs them.
suggestions.recommended_because: (A) gets the same confirmation from a machine-readable source; (B) is worth revisiting only where play-by-play and the chart disagree.

questions.question: Which price data may the site use for a market line, and is a third-party mirror acceptable for that?
questions.known: The repository has no official price source. A fingerprinted nflverse mirror carries spread/moneyline/total prices for the 2026 games (all labelled `mirror`), and the shadow baseline deliberately publishes its fair line with `market_line` and `residual` blank.
questions.missing: A decision on whether a mirror price may stand in for 'the market' in a published residual, and if so, whose book, at what timestamp, and with what label.
questions.how_to_find_out: Owner decision, one line. Nothing external is required: the two candidate labels ('mirror-derived, not official' versus 'no residual published') are both implementable today, and the mirror's own pin already fixes which bytes a number came from.
questions.unblocks: the residual column, the CLV component of scoring, every ROI figure, and gates G5/G6 on the leaderboard
questions.blocking: market line and residual on pages/line-origination.html and pages/shadow-baseline.html

questions.question: Is the results feed's closure baseline the 2026-11-14 standings snapshot or the live standings register?
questions.known: The feed is validated by reproducing W-L-T/PF/PA of the standings as read 2026-11-14, and that equality is what limits it to 137 rows. The 2026-11-16 official standings are transcribed, cross-checked against two other official pages (60 records, 0 mismatches) and proven to close against the delta (160 assertions, 0 failures).
questions.missing: Which of the two the leaderboard's data gate should read, since a rolling baseline makes the feed self-fulfilling and a frozen one freezes coverage.
questions.how_to_find_out: No new data needed — it is a policy choice about whether 'verified' is relative to a date. One line in docs/methodology, then S-22 executes it.
questions.unblocks: S-22; the `official_verified` count going from 1 to 14 for Week 10
questions.blocking: the results feed's coverage claim on pages/validation.html
questions.default_if_unanswered: frozen baseline; newer reads published as dated evidence only

questions.question: Now that every read is retained, may `data/pipeline/*.json` keep being overwritten in place?
questions.known: The register files are the collector's output and are overwritten each run; that is what left the site with one capture for five game weeks. The capture store now retains every read by content hash, so an in-place overwrite no longer destroys history — with one exception: only reads the collector actually runs get retained.
questions.missing: Whether hand-authored dated artefacts (data/nfl/*.tsv, the 2026_11_16 pack) are the canonical record and the register is a cache, or whether the register is canonical and the dated files are extracts.
questions.how_to_find_out: Answerable from the repository by choosing one and stating it; the distinction only matters the first time the two disagree (they currently do, for 23 of 32 clubs after Week 10).
questions.unblocks: which file any future checker is allowed to read, and whether the register may be re-baselined without a review
questions.blocking: every 'as of' date on the site, which is currently inherited from whichever file a given page happened to read
questions.default_if_unanswered: dated files canonical; register treated as a cache

questions.question: Is a careful hand transcription of an official page 'officially verified', or does verification require the machine read?
questions.known: The Week 10 injury pack and all three 2026-11-16 packs are hand transcriptions of official pages, each cross-checked arithmetically (standings closure, slate completeness, 32-clubs-exactly-once) and cross-compared against a second official page that prints the same records. They are the only source for several published numbers.
questions.missing: Whether the same status attaches to them as to the collector's parsed reads, and whether the site should print a distinct label for the two.
questions.how_to_find_out: Owner decision. A useful data point already in the repo: the arithmetic gates caught a transcription error of mine in this very session (a bye row written with the wrong column order, caught by the 13-column check), which is evidence the checks work — and evidence they are checks, not proof.
questions.unblocks: how the verification pages label rows, and whether 'official_verified' needs a tier
questions.blocking: the wording of every verified/unverified label on pages/validation.html
questions.default_if_unanswered: label hand transcriptions as `transcribed` beside `parsed`, both official-sourced

questions.question: What staking rule and bankroll does the leaderboard assume, if any?
questions.known: Scoring constants are registered (single win 10 / loss -11, CLV bonus 2.0 per point, breakeven 0.524 at -110) and the gates are written (100 bets official minimum, 25 provisional, binomial P(win ≤ breakeven) < 0.05, 25-unit max drawdown, 0.7 portfolio correlation cap). The brief requires signal to be separated from staking.
questions.missing: The stake itself — flat unit, fraction, or Kelly — and the bankroll the units are denominated in. Without it, no row of the leaderboard can be settled.
questions.how_to_find_out: Owner decision. The site can publish signal-only indefinitely, which is the current state and is internally consistent; anything else needs a number.
questions.unblocks: the leaderboard's economic columns and the reward mechanics
questions.blocking: every ROI, bankroll and drawdown column on pages/leaderboard.html
questions.default_if_unanswered: signal only; staking columns stay absent, not zero

questions.question: Who funds the reward pool, and is there a jurisdiction constraint?
questions.known: The pool is recorded as owner-funded and pending, and the reward rules are not written. Nothing in the repository pays out anything.
questions.missing: Funding decision, rules in writing, and a legality read for the owner's jurisdiction.
questions.how_to_find_out: Owner and, for legality, a lawyer — not a data task. Flagged so it is not mistaken for a gap in collection.
questions.unblocks: R-10 in the readiness register, and any claim that the leaderboard has stakes
questions.default_if_unanswered: the leaderboard stays a ranking with no payout

questions.question: Where does depth come from for a club whose chart the league does not publish as text?
questions.known: 31 of 32 clubs yield parseable depth from the collected source; the Texans' chart is published as an image and produced 0 slots, and four players (Chris Brooks, Micah Parsons, Skyy Moore and others) cannot be joined at all. Club sites are already an accepted host precisely because the league publishes no chart of its own.
questions.missing: Whether a club's own page is acceptable for the depth ordering that feeds the replacement matrix, given it is neither contemporaneous nor uniform in format.
questions.how_to_find_out: Owner decision on source hierarchy; mechanically, club pages are fetchable today and the deficiency matrix would then need a per-source label rather than a single 'official' column.
questions.unblocks: the backup-deficiency matrix's coverage claim, and the 0-slot exception
questions.blocking: pages/availability.html depth coverage (31/32) and the missing-player join flags
questions.default_if_unanswered: publish the hole: 31/32 with the Texans row blank and flagged

questions.question: How many consecutive days of captures are needed before a drift alarm is treated as a finding rather than as noise?
questions.known: Two dated injury reads exist (2026-11-14, 2026-11-15) and one standings delta (11-14 → 11-16). The first delta changed shape once already — 62 changed cells became 34 after the club-code alias was added — which shows the estimate moves with the join, not with the league.
questions.missing: A minimum-n rule for publishing 'the injury report moved' claims, and the same rule for the surprise-not-level signal the brief asks for.
questions.how_to_find_out: No decision needed to gather it, only time and green runs: the series is the answer. Worth stating now so the page can say 'n=2' rather than implying a trend.
questions.unblocks: S-24, PR-04's evaluation window, and any 'movement' column on the availability page
questions.default_if_unanswered: publish every delta with its n and its two dates, no rolling averages

questions.question: What are the two undocumented record triples and the duplicate win-percentage columns on the standings page?
questions.known: The page's own legend defines W L T PCT HOME ROAD DIV CONF PF PA NET PTS STRK. The table prints two further record triples and a second PCT column; `data/pipeline/standings.json` carries 18 printed columns including two columns both headed `Pct`. This session did not transcribe the undocumented ones.
questions.missing: A definition. Publishing 'DIV' or 'CONF' as a division or conference record without the page saying so would be inference, and the arithmetic check that closes W-L-T does not extend to columns whose meaning is assumed.
questions.how_to_find_out: Two candidate answers are cheap to test: NFL Operations' definitions page, or reproducing each undocumented triple from the schedule for one club and seeing which subset of games it equals. The second is arithmetic, needs no new source, and can be done here — it is listed as a suggestion the moment anyone has an hour.
questions.unblocks: whether the standings table on the site is complete or a subset
questions.blocking: nothing published today, because the columns are simply absent — which is the correct outcome while the question is open
questions.default_if_unanswered: leave the undocumented columns out of the published table

questions.question: Does a blank cell on a mid-week read mean 'no designation', or 'the page had not been published yet'?
questions.known: The `game_status` column is legitimately blank most days — the injury report has no Monday or Saturday edition — so the pin allows up to 95% blank and only alarms above that. It also means a field that vanished entirely could hide inside a generous allowance.
questions.missing: The publishing calendar, stated as data (which days the league posts which report), so the allowance can be day-specific instead of one fixed fraction.
questions.how_to_find_out: Derivable from the captures themselves once a fortnight of them exists — the blank-fraction by weekday is a histogram this repository will be able to print from its own index, with no new source.
questions.unblocks: tightening `blank-over-allowance` from an alarm to a gate without firing on Wednesdays
questions.blocking: the strength of the injury-drift gate
questions.default_if_unanswered: keep the generous allowance, alarm-only, with the reason on the page

executive_summary.what: The collector was healthy and landed nothing for a week.
executive_summary.detail: Every scheduled run exited 0 while its own commit log recorded a push that failed five times: the commit step deleted two tracked log files and left the deletions unstaged, and `git rebase` refuses a dirty tree. The workflow now restores them, rebases with `--autostash`, and fails loudly if it cannot push.

executive_summary.what: Retention exists, so a read is no longer overwritten by the next read.
executive_summary.detail: 9 captures over 7 datasets, content-addressed, with 2 published alarms and 0 integrity failures; day-over-day injury and standings deltas became computable for the first time (34 changed cells; 184 standings cells).

executive_summary.what: Week 10 and Week 11 are now transcribed from the official pages, with closure proved.
executive_summary.detail: 13 finals + 1 unplayed fixture; 32-club standings cross-checked against two other official pages (60 records, 0 mismatches) and against the delta that reproduces them (160 assertions, 0 failures). The published 2026-11-14 tables were left as dated artefacts rather than rewritten.

executive_summary.what: PR-01 is registered, scored, and started.
executive_summary.detail: Brier 0.224 on 117 chronologically held-out games, +0.116 skill against the 0.55 home baseline with a +0.002 lower bound; hit rate 0.641; realised wins 75 against 76.1 expected (z = -0.21), i.e. the record is exactly what its own model expects of luck. 14 pre-kickoff forecasts are now frozen.

executive_summary.what: The site's own claim of verified Week 10 coverage is still 1 of 14, on purpose.
executive_summary.detail: Closing that gap means moving the transcription, the row-count pin, the standings baseline and the mirror pin in one commit; appending in isolation breaks 23 of 32 clubs against the baseline the feed is validated by. That is S-22 and Q-62.
